title: Determination that Flock's transparency-portal possession/publication of SMPD ALPR data is "data hosting" under §1798.90.55(b)
summary: Asks for any record reflecting a determination that Flock Safety's possession and publication of the Department's ALPR search-audit information on the transparency portal constitutes "data hosting" under Civil Code § 1798.90.55(b), rather than a sale, sharing, or transfer of that information to Flock Safety. Filed the same day as, and directly quoting, W013438's Item 1 answer: "The Flock Safety transparency portal is maintained by Flock Safety. The Department does not maintain a separate screenshot, printout, or export of the 'Prohibited Uses' section outside of the information available on the portal."

policy_promises.quote: the provision of data hosting or towing services shall not be considered the sale, sharing, or transferring of ALPR information
policy_promises.tests: Whether the Department has any documented determination that Flock's possession and public display of SMPD's ALPR search-audit data on the transparency portal is lawful under the hosting carve-out — the only apparent lawful basis if the portal is, as the Department stated, "maintained by Flock Safety" and not the Department itself.

prior_pra_refs.note: 9/21/2026 Item 1 response — "The Flock Safety transparency portal is maintained by Flock Safety" — is the statement this request tests against § 1798.90.55(b).
Produced Flock platform event-log data, cited elsewhere (W013278) as evidence records held by Flock as SMPD's contractor are City records.

filed_because: SMPD's W013438 answer characterized the transparency portal as Flock's, not the Department's. Civil Code § 1798.90.55(b) permits ALPR information to reach a vendor only via a sale/sharing/transfer to another public agency, or via a "data hosting" carve-out that isn't considered a sale, sharing, or transfer at all. If the portal genuinely isn't the Department's, the lawful basis for Flock's possession and public display of SMPD's ALPR search-audit data there needs to be something other than hosting on the Department's behalf — this asks whether any such determination has ever been made.
notes: Filed 2026-09-21. Statutory 10-day initial determination due 2026-10-01 (Gov. Code § 7922.535(a)).
